recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not restore or duplicate obsolete patient-as-entity wording for FHIR-23835; any future cleanup belongs to the later AuditEvent.patient issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-23835 was a Published/Persuasive Security change request asking for AuditEvent guidance that patient/subject references should be included for auditable events when possible, plus matching Security module text, examples, and possible profile work.
initial_application: HL7/fhir PR #708, merged as e5f777ad514d570245abf181a3637f154a2529a9 on 2019-10-03, initially applied the issue by adding an AuditEvent patient-subject section using the then-current AuditEvent.entity representation, adding the linked Security module Accounting of Disclosures sentence, and touching AuditEvent examples.
additional_context: FHIR-33155 later reached Published/Persuasive with Modification and intentionally moved the patient-subject representation to a first-class AuditEvent.patient element; commit 4af66cb9b0e7b2d14f39a4eecfb660d55ff964c9 added that element, search-parameter wiring, examples, and updated the #patient narrative. FHIR-36144 confirmed that the #patient section now speaks to .patient rather than entity.who. The Zulip discussion behind FHIR-23835 framed this as best-practice guidance with reasonable-effort exceptions, and no Confluence reference was found that changes the conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. AuditEvent is active in source/fhir.ini, and current source already conveys the requested rule through AuditEvent.patient, the AuditEvent notes section, the Security and Privacy module link, and examples using AuditEvent.patient.
